summary: The note describes the 2010 United States House of Representatives elections, in which Republicans regained control of the chamber by a net gain of 63 seats, erasing Democratic gains from 2006 and 2008. It calls the result the largest midterm loss for a president's party since 1938 and the largest House swing since 1948, with New York state the biggest source of Republican gains. It attributes Democratic losses to anger with President Obama, opposition to the Affordable Care Act, large budget deficits and the weak economy, and lists notable freshmen who later held major offices. The source is a duplicated wiki text, and the two copies differ on Mike Pompeo's later post (Secretary of State in one, CIA director in the other).
one_line: Summary of the 2010 US House elections, in which Republicans regained the chamber with a net gain of 63 seats.
key_facts: Republicans regained control of the U.S. House of Representatives in the 2010 elections, which they had lost in the 2006 midterm elections.
Republicans picked up a net total of 63 House seats in the 2010 elections.
The 2010 election erased the House gains Democrats made in 2006 and 2008.
The 2010 election produced the highest loss of a party in a House midterm election since 1938.
The 2010 election produced the largest House swing since 1948.
The 2010 election was the Republicans' largest gain in House seats since 1938.
Republicans gained the most in New York state, where they picked up six seats.
In New York, Republicans defeated five incumbents and won an open Democratic district.
Democratic losses were attributed to anger with President Obama, opposition to the Affordable Care Act, large budget deficits and the weak economy.
The 2010 election was the third consecutive midterm election in a president's first term in which Republicans made House gains.
The 2010 election was the second consecutive midterm in which party control of the House changed hands.
Notable 2010 freshmen included future Senators Cory Gardner, Todd Young, James Lankford and Tim Scott.
Notable 2010 freshmen included future Governor of Delaware John Carney and future Director of the Office of Management and Budget Mick Mulvaney.
Notable 2010 freshmen included Mike Pompeo, described in one copy as future Secretary of State and in the other as future CIA director.
Notable 2010 freshmen included future Lieutenant Governor of Arkansas Tim Griffin and future Louisiana Attorney General Jeff Landry.
